waves.fact: INSPIRE ID relates a polygon to a registered title, but one title may have several polygons and INSPIRE is indicative only.
waves.guard: Never promote INSPIRE ID/polygon alone to exact legal boundary.

waves.fact: Local-authority boundary polygons can appear in two authority GML files; July 2026 files are monthly snapshots.
waves.guard: Deduplicate stable polygon identity and preserve authority-file/month provenance.

waves.fact: HMLR INSPIRE is native British National Grid/EPSG:27700; HMLR warns BNG→WGS84 conversion may shift some features up to 15m.
waves.guard: Use native BNG for matching and fail closed on uncontrolled reprojection.

waves.fact: INSPIRE geometry is OGL reusable with required HMLR/OS attribution and dated monthly publication.
waves.guard: Persist publication date, source file and attribution; licence is not precision evidence.

waves.fact: Ordinary title plans/general boundaries do not record the exact legal line; determined boundaries do.
waves.guard: Do not use ordinary title-plan red edging as exact sample geometry.

waves.fact: Determined plan needs clear extent, endpoints/turning points, OS-relatable context, orientation and stated scale.
waves.guard: Reject ambiguous, unscaled or 'identification only' geometry.

waves.fact: Determined-plan measurements must be horizontal, +/-10mm and controlled from at least two permanent points.
waves.guard: Reject slope distance, single control point or decay-prone controls.

waves.fact: Coordinate-based determined plans accept National Grid coordinates at +/-300mm absolute and +/-10mm relative accuracy.
waves.guard: Reject non-National-Grid or uncertified coordinate control.

waves.fact: EA Composite DTM 1m uses multiple surveys and metadata index lineage; some inputs are bilinearly resampled.
waves.guard: Require contributing-survey metadata for each sample.

waves.fact: EA Composite DTM is 5km GeoTIFF, metres, ODN/Newlyn, OSTN15, EPSG:27700, input survey vertical accuracy +/-15cm RMSE.
waves.guard: Do not subtract heights without compatible datum/tile provenance.

waves.fact: EA Time Stamped DTM spans surveys since 1998 at 25cm–2m; transformation is survey-period specific.
waves.guard: Require survey date, resolution and transformation for historic samples.

waves.fact: EA point cloud may not match every historic raster; classified ground can differ from manually edited final DTM.
waves.guard: Use point cloud as supplementary lineage/cross-check, not automatic DTM replacement.

waves.fact: EA DTM removes surface objects; DSM includes buildings/vegetation.
waves.guard: Reject DSM/object height as bare-earth parcel elevation.

waves.fact: EA raster products use 5km OS-grid tiles and candidate geometry can cross tile edges.
waves.guard: Sample every verified intersected tile and record deterministic pixel/sample locator.

waves.fact: OS Terrain 5 is a 5m DTM, 5km tiles, quarterly updates, typical accuracy greater than 2m RMSE.
waves.guard: Use as secondary coarse cross-check; never as centimetre-precision evidence.

waves.fact: HMLR and EA evidence can be matched natively in EPSG:27700/OS grid.
waves.guard: Reject silent CRS mixing or web-map snapping before raster sampling.

waves.fact: EA heights are ODN/Newlyn; historic Time Stamped transformations can differ by survey period.
waves.guard: Reject subtraction across unresolved vertical datum/transform lineage.

waves.fact: Boundary-control, reprojection and elevation errors are separate components; resolution is not accuracy.
waves.guard: Report conservative combined uncertainty and reject false decimal precision.

waves.fact: Canonical status records 3 candidate rows, but wrapper exposes no real candidate identifiers; wrapper only decodes compressed payload.
waves.guard: Do not invent title numbers, coordinates or polygons; keep 3 candidate identities unresolved.

waves.fact: Revision-14 runtime and integrity outputs are still absent and the existing single runner remains blocked behind height_difference_2 recovery.
waves.guard: Do not create a second runner/task or promote numeric output before both remote outputs exist.
